title: Alkem Laboratories Ltd - 539523 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Alkem Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~11% to INR3,740 crores, but net profit fell 21.7% on tax; Trade Generics flattish and Daman OAI flagged.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew close to 11% YoY to INR3,740 crores, with India sales up 10.3% to INR2,497 crores and International up 16% to INR1,222 crores. EBITDA margin was 20.5% (EBITDA growth 3.7% YoY), PBT rose about 1.8%, and net profit fell 21.7%, which management attributed to taxation. Management said the company outperformed the IPM by 100 bps (13.2% vs 12.2%, per IQVIA), but Trade Generics were flattish in April-June. The Daman facility received an OAI status from the US FDA, which management said does not affect supplies this year.

segments.name: India formulations
segments.commentary: Grew 10.3% to INR2,497 crores; IQVIA-tracked growth 13.2% vs IPM 12.2%. Acute grew 12.3% (vs IPM 10.1%) and chronic 17.9% (vs IPM 15.4%). Branded generics grew 12%, while Trade Generics were flattish to mildly up.

segments.name: India price/volume (ex-Trade Generics)
segments.commentary: Price up ~6%, new launches ~3%, volume ~2%. Seven biosimilars launched in India generate about INR150 crores annual sales.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,222 crores, up 16% YoY. Management cited Germany growing 35-40% on a small base, and Chile and Australia performing well.

segments.name: US CDMO (Enzene, mAbs)
segments.commentary: Operational expense about INR60 crores per quarter; operational since November 2025. Management said breakeven needs roughly USD25-30 million annualised revenue, expected in FY27-FY28 rather than within 12 months.

segments.name: MedTech / Occlutech
segments.commentary: Occlutech acquisition completed mid-July 2026, so not in Q1. Ex-diligence and Occlutech, MedTech EBITDA loss was about INR5-7 crores. FY27 Occlutech target about INR400 crores sales (8.5 months) at breakeven EBITDA.

guidance_outlook: US business: high single digit to mid growth for FY27, helped by currency; price erosion described as roughly flat.
India overall (Trade Generics plus branded): full-year growth close to the prior guidance, could be better by about 100 bps; management said close to 12% is achievable.
Gross margin maintained at 66.5-67% for the balance of FY27, with API price increases expected to weigh in subsequent quarters.
Occlutech: EBITDA margin to improve about 7-8% YoY, targeting full guidance within 3-4 years; FY27 breakeven.
US CDMO breakeven targeted in roughly 4-5 quarters per Nitin Agrawal, but Sandeep Singh said it will not break even in the next 12 months.
Trade Generics: management is comfortable with late single-digit growth and wants 1-2 years of execution and discipline.
Denosumab biosimilar US approval delayed by at least a few months after the goal date; Xgeva biosimilar Europe launch about 3 months away.
capex_capacity: Daman facility (US) received OAI status; CAPA initiated and engagement with the regulator ongoing. Daman accounts for about 45% of US revenue, and management said supplies continue without interruption.
US CDMO (Enzene, mAbs) has small but technology-intensive capacity that is not US FDA approved yet; capex will be needed later for scale but not this year.
Cash balance cited at INR5,700 crores; no change to capital allocation plans and no acquisitions planned in orthopaedics or MedTech.
Five US ANDA approvals in the quarter, one of them tentative.
demand_pricing: Trade Generics were flattish in April-June after a higher single-digit rise in Jan-June. Reasons: intense competition, tighter receivable (DSO) discipline, and API-driven price increases that reduced channel inventory.
India price growth about 6% ex-Trade Generics, volume about 2%, new launches about 3%.
Management said the chronic IPM was helped by semaglutide going off-patent, though the direct benefit to Alkem is small. Alkem is claimed to be among the top 3 in generics.
Outperformed IPM in 7 focus therapies: anti-infectives 1.1x, gastro 1.2x, vitamins and minerals 1.4x, pain 1.8x, antidiabetic 1.4x, respiratory 1.6x, derma 1.6x.
US: no meaningful volume growth on recent launches; growth driven by currency. Price erosion described as flattish.
Gross margin improved in Q1 due to a better mix (lower Trade Generics, stronger prescription business) and currency support, while old inventory cost helped.

qa_highlights.question: Why is India growth (10.3%) lagging peers, and what is driving it?
qa_highlights.answer: Trade Generics were flattish to mildly up and dragged the India number; branded generics grew 12%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 16%+ employee cost growth and other expenses, and what are the Enzene CDMO and MedTech losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee costs rose over 16% due to increments, about 1,200 MRs added over recent quarters and Enzene operations from November 2025. Other expenses rose with foreign subsidiary costs ~10% higher. Ex-Occlutech and diligence, MedTech EBITDA loss was about INR5-7 crores. US CDMO opex about INR60 crores per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Trade Generics outlook and what is the reason for weak growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition has intensified and tighter DSO practices were applied. Management expects late single-digit growth as acceptable and needs 1-2 years of discipline; Q1 primary sales should recover in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone guided 27-28%; consolidated is expected at 30-32% because loss-making entities such as US Enzene carry no deferred tax asset.

qa_highlights.question: Daman OAI impact and share of US revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Daman supplies about 45% of US revenue. Management expects no impact on business this year and recovery within 6-12 months; US FY27 guidance raised to high single digit to mid.

qa_highlights.question: Denosumab biosimilar status and Europe plans?
qa_highlights.answer: US approval missed the goal date and is delayed by a few months. Europe Prolia partnered with Theramex, with a competitive market and no meaningful ramp soon. Xgeva European launch is about 3 months away.

qa_highlights.question: Occlutech targets and margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 (8.5 months) target is about INR400 crores sales at breakeven EBITDA, below earlier guidance due to integration delays. Margins expected to improve gradually over 3-4 years.

risks_watch: US Daman facility OAI status: CAPA is in progress, and resolution is expected in 6-12 months; watch for any impact on US supplies.
Trade Generics growth recovery is uncertain given competition and DSO tightening; watch the Q2 print.
Consolidated tax rate of 30-32% and the 21.7% fall in net profit suggest continued pressure below EBITDA.
API price increases may pressure gross margin in subsequent quarters, against the 66.5-67% guidance.
US CDMO needs about USD25-30 million annualised revenue to break even, with a lumpy sales cycle and FY28 timing; Enzene is not yet US FDA approved.
Denosumab biosimilar US approval delay; competitive Europe launch.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India outperformance and International growth, but cautious and somewhat evasive on Trade Generics, CDMO timelines and the Daman OAI impact. Management gave answers that changed during the call, such as the CDMO breakeven timeline and the US growth guidance.

growth.why: India growth guided at about 12% for FY27, could be ~100 bps better, backed by IQVIA-tracked outperformance (13.2% vs IPM 12.2%) and ~6% price, ~2% volume, ~3% launches; US guided high single digit to mid growth (cut), Trade Generics flattish, and Occlutech adds ~INR400 crore FY27 sales from mid-July acquisition.
